1.1.text:
WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is the Konawe Kepulauan Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of Konawe Kepulauan Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Konawe Kepulauan.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Konawe Kepulauan Regency.
5. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, -4- social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
6. Woman is a person who has female genitalia, can experience menstruation, pregnancy, childbirth, breastfeeding and includes persons who are legally recognized as Women.
7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child in the womb.
8. Violence is any act against a person that results in suffering or pain physically, sexually, psychologically, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty.
9. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or pain to women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or private life.
10. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in suffering or pain physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty.
11. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, serious injury or disability to a person's body, miscarriage or unconsciousness and/or causes death.
12. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, distrust or severe psychological suffering to a person.
13. Sexual violence is any act in the form of forced sexual intercourse, sexual abuse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural and/or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
14. Exploitation is an action with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or -5- body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain material or immaterial benefits.
15. Victim is a woman and child who experiences physical suffering, psychological suffering, sexual suffering, either directly or indirectly resulting from acts of violence.
16. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
18. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
19. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by Professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
20. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for strengthening victims of violence to resolve the problems they face.
21. Repatriation is an effort to return women and children victims of violence to their families or communities that can provide protection and fulfill their needs.
22. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions so that they can carry out their roles normally both in the family and in society.
23. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with their families, communities, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection and fulfill the needs of victims.
24. Institution is an agency/office/body/office within the scope of regional government and/or non-governmental organizations that provide assistance.
25. Integrated Service Center hereinafter referred to as PPT is a generic term that can be used by various institutions that provide services for victims of violence such as Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, Safe House, Child Social Protection House, Trauma Center Protection House, Women's Social Protection House, Shelter, etc.
26. Minimum Service Standards hereinafter abbreviated as SPM is a performance benchmark for integrated service units in providing services for handling reports/complaints, health services, Social Rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal assistance, as well as Repatriation and social reintegration for Women and Children Victims of Violence. 27. Regional Action Plan is a foundation and guideline for relevant agencies, vertical agencies, and the community, in carrying out activities for the implementation of prevention and protection of women and children victims of violence.
28. Safe House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards.

Article 19

1. The Integrated Service Center in carrying out its duties and functions may coordinate with the Sub-district Integrated Service Center, and competent parties in making efforts to prevent violence against women and children.

14- (2) Further provisions regarding the mechanism for implementing prevention duties as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Every citizen has the right to be free from torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and has the right to obtain a sense of security and freedom from all forms of violence. Violence is any act against a person that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty.

Women and children are groups vulnerable to experiencing violence. All forms of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity, therefore legal protection is needed to protect their dignity and to guarantee their right to life in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.

This view is based on Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia which states that "Every person has the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under their control, and has the right to a sense of security and protection from threats of fear to do or not do something which is a human right".

The Regional Government is obliged and responsible to implement efforts to protect women and children victims of violence through implementing protection policies for women and children victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence, establishing PPT, ensuring -2- the implementation of service facilities for victims, seeking effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and seeking the creation of cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Konawe Kepulauan Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of services, assistance, guidance, supervision, reporting and funding for women and children victims of violence in Konawe Kepulauan Regency.

Article 13

The obligations of family and parents as referred to in Article 10 letter c, who legally have full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence and protect women and children as part of family members.
11-

Article 14

1. In order to provide services and protection to women and children from violence, the Regional Government establishes an Integrated Service Center as a service center for women and children victims of violence.
2. The Integrated Service Center as referred to in paragraph (1), consists of elements of the Office of Population Control Family Planning Women's Protection and Child Protection, Health Office, Education and Culture Office, Social Office, Population and Civil Registration Administration Office, Community and Village Empowerment Office, Civil Service Police Unit, Regional General Hospital, Police Resort, Non-Governmental Organizations, and Universities.
3. The Integrated Service Center as referred to in paragraph (2), is established by Regent's Decree.
4. Further provisions regarding the organizational structure of the Integrated Service Center are regulated by Regent's Regulation.

Article 25

Guidance and supervision as referred to in Article 24 paragraph (2) and paragraph (3), are carried out in order to realize the objectives of implementing protection for women and children victims of violence in accordance with minimum service standards established by laws and regulations.

Article 28

1. The Regional Government may provide financial assistance to community organizations, social organizations, or non-governmental organizations and universities that implement protection for women and children victims of violence.
2. Financial assistance as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be in accordance with regional financial capacity and implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations in the field of regional finance.

CHAPTER IV

RIGHTS OF VICTIMS

Article 10

Every victim has the right to obtain:
a. protection from individuals, groups and institutions both government and non-government.
b. access and information about the existence of complaint centers, PPT, and all matters related to the fulfillment of their rights and involvement in the decision-making process related to assistance and case development.
c. services that include medical, extensive medicolegal, psychosocial and legal.
9-
d. handling that does not stop until physical and psychological healing, but until the victim can resume life in society including the restoration of their good name.
f. confidential handling which includes guarantees for the victim that their identity will not be disseminated, medical care and legal handling.

assistance provided by psychologists to victims suffering from trauma/other mental problems to restore the victim's mental condition.
g. legal aid assistance provided by persons and/or legal aid institutions to victims at every level of examination and during the legal process.
h. guarantees of rights related to the victim's status

CHAPTER V

OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Article 10

Obligations and responsibilities in the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence are the shared responsibility of:
a. regional government;
b. society;
c. family and parents.

Article 21

15- (2) The mechanism for implementing duties as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be organized according to Standard Operating Procedures which are further regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 18

Integrated Service CenterForms of prevention of violence against women and children carried out by the Integrated Service Center, can be implemented through:
a. socialization activities of laws and regulations to the community related to the protection of the rights of women and children; andb. training of Integrated Service Center members related to the implementation of their duties in preventing violence against children and women.

I. GENERAL

Every citizen has the right to be free from torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and has the right to obtain a sense of security and freedom from all forms of violence. Violence is any act against a person that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty.

Women and children are groups vulnerable to experiencing violence. All forms of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity, therefore legal protection is needed to protect their dignity and to guarantee their right to life in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.

This view is based on Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia which states that "Every person has the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under their control, and has the right to a sense of security and protection from threats of fear to do or not do something which is a human right".

The Regional Government is obliged and responsible to implement efforts to protect women and children victims of violence through implementing protection policies for women and children victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence, establishing PPT, ensuring -2- the implementation of service facilities for victims, seeking effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and seeking the creation of cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Konawe Kepulauan Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Every citizen has the right to be free from torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and has the right to obtain a sense of security and freedom from all forms of violence. Violence is any act against a person that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty.

Women and children are groups vulnerable to experiencing violence. All forms of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity, therefore legal protection is needed to protect their dignity and to guarantee their right to life in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.

This view is based on Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia which states that "Every person has the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under their control, and has the right to a sense of security and protection from threats of fear to do or not do something which is a human right".

The Regional Government is obliged and responsible to implement efforts to protect women and children victims of violence through implementing protection policies for women and children victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence, establishing PPT, ensuring -2- the implementation of service facilities for victims, seeking effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and seeking the creation of cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Konawe Kepulauan Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of services, assistance, guidance, supervision, reporting and funding for women and children victims of violence in Konawe Kepulauan Regency.

Article 14

1. In order to provide services and protection to women and children from violence, the Regional Government establishes an Integrated Service Center as a service center for women and children victims of violence.
2. The Integrated Service Center as referred to in paragraph (1), consists of elements of the Office of Population Control Family Planning Women's Protection and Child Protection, Health Office, Education and Culture Office, Social Office, Population and Civil Registration Administration Office, Community and Village Empowerment Office, Civil Service Police Unit, Regional General Hospital, Police Resort, Non-Governmental Organizations, and Universities.
3. The Integrated Service Center as referred to in paragraph (2), is established by Regent's Decree.
4. Further provisions regarding the organizational structure of the Integrated Service Center are regulated by Regent's Regulation.

Article 21

1. In carrying out the task of providing services to women and children victims of violence, the Integrated Service Center coordinates with the Sub-district Integrated Service Center.

15- (2) The mechanism for implementing duties as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be organized according to Standard Operating Procedures which are further regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 13

The obligations of family and parents as referred to in Article 10 letter c, who legally have full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence and protect women and children as part of family members.

Article 28

1. The Regional Government may provide financial assistance to community organizations, social organizations, or non-governmental organizations and universities that implement protection for women and children victims of violence.
2. Financial assistance as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be in accordance with regional financial capacity and implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations in the field of regional finance.

Obligations and responsibilities in the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence are the shared responsibility of:

b. finance;
c. services; andd. performance.
3. Submission of written reports as referred to in paragraph (2), shall be carried out at least once every 3 (three) months.

7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child in the womb.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is the Konawe Kepulauan Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of Konawe Kepulauan Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Konawe Kepulauan.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Konawe Kepulauan Regency.
5. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, -4- social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
6. Woman is a person who has female genitalia, can experience menstruation, pregnancy, childbirth, breastfeeding and includes persons who are legally recognized as Women.
7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child in the womb.
8. Violence is any act against a person that results in suffering or pain physically, sexually, psychologically, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty.
9. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or pain to women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or private life.
10. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in suffering or pain physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty.
11. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, serious injury or disability to a person's body, miscarriage or unconsciousness and/or causes death.
12. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, distrust or severe psychological suffering to a person.
13. Sexual violence is any act in the form of forced sexual intercourse, sexual abuse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural and/or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
14. Exploitation is an action with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or -5- body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain material or immaterial benefits.
15. Victim is a woman and child who experiences physical suffering, psychological suffering, sexual suffering, either directly or indirectly resulting from acts of violence.
16. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
18. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
19. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by Professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
20. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for strengthening victims of violence to resolve the problems they face.
21. Repatriation is an effort to return women and children victims of violence to their families or communities that can provide protection and fulfill their needs.
22. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions so that they can carry out their roles normally both in the family and in society.
23. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with their families, communities, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection and fulfill the needs of victims.
24. Institution is an agency/office/body/office within the scope of regional government and/or non-governmental organizations that provide assistance.
25. Integrated Service Center hereinafter referred to as PPT is a generic term that can be used by various institutions that provide services for victims of violence such as Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, Safe House, Child Social Protection House, Trauma Center Protection House, Women's Social Protection House, Shelter, etc.
26. Minimum Service Standards hereinafter abbreviated as SPM is a performance benchmark for integrated service units in providing services for handling reports/complaints, health services, Social Rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal assistance, as well as Repatriation and social reintegration for Women and Children Victims of Violence. 27. Regional Action Plan is a foundation and guideline for relevant agencies, vertical agencies, and the community, in carrying out activities for the implementation of prevention and protection of women and children victims of violence.
28. Safe House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards.

3. The Integrated Service Center as referred to in paragraph (2), is established by Regent's Decree.
4. Further provisions regarding the organizational structure of the Integrated Service Center are regulated by Regent's Regulation.

Article 21

15- (2) The mechanism for implementing duties as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be organized according to Standard Operating Procedures which are further regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 19

14- (2) Further provisions regarding the mechanism for implementing prevention duties as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Every citizen has the right to be free from torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and has the right to obtain a sense of security and freedom from all forms of violence. Violence is any act against a person that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty.

Women and children are groups vulnerable to experiencing violence. All forms of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity, therefore legal protection is needed to protect their dignity and to guarantee their right to life in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.

This view is based on Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia which states that "Every person has the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under their control, and has the right to a sense of security and protection from threats of fear to do or not do something which is a human right".

The Regional Government is obliged and responsible to implement efforts to protect women and children victims of violence through implementing protection policies for women and children victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence, establishing PPT, ensuring -2- the implementation of service facilities for victims, seeking effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and seeking the creation of cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Konawe Kepulauan Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of services, assistance, guidance, supervision, reporting and funding for women and children victims of violence in Konawe Kepulauan Regency.

Article 28

1. The Regional Government may provide financial assistance to community organizations, social organizations, or non-governmental organizations and universities that implement protection for women and children victims of violence.
2. Financial assistance as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be in accordance with regional financial capacity and implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations in the field of regional finance.

Article 25

Guidance and supervision as referred to in Article 24 paragraph (2) and paragraph (3), are carried out in order to realize the objectives of implementing protection for women and children victims of violence in accordance with minimum service standards established by laws and regulations.

CHAPTER IX

FUNDING

Article 27

Funds for the implementation of protection of women and children victims of violence, are sourced from:
a. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget; andb. other lawful sources in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Every citizen has the right to be free from torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and has the right to obtain a sense of security and freedom from all forms of violence. Violence is any act against a person that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty.

Women and children are groups vulnerable to experiencing violence. All forms of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity, therefore legal protection is needed to protect their dignity and to guarantee their right to life in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.

This view is based on Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia which states that "Every person has the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under their control, and has the right to a sense of security and protection from threats of fear to do or not do something which is a human right".

The Regional Government is obliged and responsible to implement efforts to protect women and children victims of violence through implementing protection policies for women and children victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence, establishing PPT, ensuring -2- the implementation of service facilities for victims, seeking effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and seeking the creation of cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Konawe Kepulauan Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of services, assistance, guidance, supervision, reporting and funding for women and children victims of violence in Konawe Kepulauan Regency.

c. services that include medical, extensive medicolegal, psychosocial and legal.

Every citizen has the right to be free from torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and has the right to obtain a sense of security and freedom from all forms of violence. Violence is any act against a person that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty.

Women and children are groups vulnerable to experiencing violence. All forms of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity, therefore legal protection is needed to protect their dignity and to guarantee their right to life in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.

This view is based on Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia which states that "Every person has the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under their control, and has the right to a sense of security and protection from threats of fear to do or not do something which is a human right".

The Regional Government is obliged and responsible to implement efforts to protect women and children victims of violence through implementing protection policies for women and children victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence, establishing PPT, ensuring -2- the implementation of service facilities for victims, seeking effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and seeking the creation of cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Konawe Kepulauan Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of services, assistance, guidance, supervision, reporting and funding for women and children victims of violence in Konawe Kepulauan Regency.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is the Konawe Kepulauan Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of Konawe Kepulauan Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Konawe Kepulauan.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Konawe Kepulauan Regency.
5. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, -4- social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
6. Woman is a person who has female genitalia, can experience menstruation, pregnancy, childbirth, breastfeeding and includes persons who are legally recognized as Women.
7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child in the womb.
8. Violence is any act against a person that results in suffering or pain physically, sexually, psychologically, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty.
9. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or pain to women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or private life.
10. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in suffering or pain physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty.
11. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, serious injury or disability to a person's body, miscarriage or unconsciousness and/or causes death.
12. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, distrust or severe psychological suffering to a person.
13. Sexual violence is any act in the form of forced sexual intercourse, sexual abuse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural and/or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
14. Exploitation is an action with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or -5- body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain material or immaterial benefits.
15. Victim is a woman and child who experiences physical suffering, psychological suffering, sexual suffering, either directly or indirectly resulting from acts of violence.
16. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
18. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
19. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by Professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
20. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for strengthening victims of violence to resolve the problems they face.
21. Repatriation is an effort to return women and children victims of violence to their families or communities that can provide protection and fulfill their needs.
22. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions so that they can carry out their roles normally both in the family and in society.
23. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with their families, communities, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection and fulfill the needs of victims.
24. Institution is an agency/office/body/office within the scope of regional government and/or non-governmental organizations that provide assistance.
25. Integrated Service Center hereinafter referred to as PPT is a generic term that can be used by various institutions that provide services for victims of violence such as Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, Safe House, Child Social Protection House, Trauma Center Protection House, Women's Social Protection House, Shelter, etc.
26. Minimum Service Standards hereinafter abbreviated as SPM is a performance benchmark for integrated service units in providing services for handling reports/complaints, health services, Social Rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal assistance, as well as Repatriation and social reintegration for Women and Children Victims of Violence. 27. Regional Action Plan is a foundation and guideline for relevant agencies, vertical agencies, and the community, in carrying out activities for the implementation of prevention and protection of women and children victims of violence.
28. Safe House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards.

The Regional Government is obliged and responsible to implement efforts to protect women and children victims of violence through implementing protection policies for women and children victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence, establishing PPT, ensuring -2- the implementation of service facilities for victims, seeking effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and seeking the creation of cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Konawe Kepulauan Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

6. Woman is a person who has female genitalia, can experience menstruation, pregnancy, childbirth, breastfeeding and includes persons who are legally recognized as Women.
7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child in the womb.
8. Violence is any act against a person that results in suffering or pain physically, sexually, psychologically, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty.
9. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or pain to women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or private life.
10. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in suffering or pain physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty.
11. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, serious injury or disability to a person's body, miscarriage or unconsciousness and/or causes death.
12. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, distrust or severe psychological suffering to a person.
13. Sexual violence is any act in the form of forced sexual intercourse, sexual abuse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural and/or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
14. Exploitation is an action with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or -5- body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain material or immaterial benefits.
15. Victim is a woman and child who experiences physical suffering, psychological suffering, sexual suffering, either directly or indirectly resulting from acts of violence.
16. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Every citizen has the right to be free from torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and has the right to obtain a sense of security and freedom from all forms of violence. Violence is any act against a person that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty.

Women and children are groups vulnerable to experiencing violence. All forms of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity, therefore legal protection is needed to protect their dignity and to guarantee their right to life in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.

This view is based on Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia which states that "Every person has the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under their control, and has the right to a sense of security and protection from threats of fear to do or not do something which is a human right".

The Regional Government is obliged and responsible to implement efforts to protect women and children victims of violence through implementing protection policies for women and children victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence, establishing PPT, ensuring -2- the implementation of service facilities for victims, seeking effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and seeking the creation of cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Konawe Kepulauan Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of services, assistance, guidance, supervision, reporting and funding for women and children victims of violence in Konawe Kepulauan Regency.

Article 28

1. The Regional Government may provide financial assistance to community organizations, social organizations, or non-governmental organizations and universities that implement protection for women and children victims of violence.
2. Financial assistance as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be in accordance with regional financial capacity and implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations in the field of regional finance.

Article 25

Guidance and supervision as referred to in Article 24 paragraph (2) and paragraph (3), are carried out in order to realize the objectives of implementing protection for women and children victims of violence in accordance with minimum service standards established by laws and regulations.

CHAPTER V

OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Article 10

Obligations and responsibilities in the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence are the shared responsibility of:
a. regional government;
b. society;
c. family and parents.

Article 21

1. In carrying out the task of providing services to women and children victims of violence, the Integrated Service Center coordinates with the Sub-district Integrated Service Center.

15- (2) The mechanism for implementing duties as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be organized according to Standard Operating Procedures which are further regulated by Regent Regulation.

CHAPTER IX

FUNDING

Article 27

Funds for the implementation of protection of women and children victims of violence, are sourced from:
a. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget; andb. other lawful sources in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

6. Woman is a person who has female genitalia, can experience menstruation, pregnancy, childbirth, breastfeeding and includes persons who are legally recognized as Women.
7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child in the womb.
8. Violence is any act against a person that results in suffering or pain physically, sexually, psychologically, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty.
9. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or pain to women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or private life.
10. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in suffering or pain physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty.
11. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, serious injury or disability to a person's body, miscarriage or unconsciousness and/or causes death.
12. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, distrust or severe psychological suffering to a person.
13. Sexual violence is any act in the form of forced sexual intercourse, sexual abuse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural and/or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
14. Exploitation is an action with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or -5- body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain material or immaterial benefits.
15. Victim is a woman and child who experiences physical suffering, psychological suffering, sexual suffering, either directly or indirectly resulting from acts of violence.
16. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
18. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother.

21. Repatriation is an effort to return women and children victims of violence to their families or communities that can provide protection and fulfill their needs.
22. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions so that they can carry out their roles normally both in the family and in society.
23. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with their families, communities, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection and fulfill the needs of victims.
24. Institution is an agency/office/body/office within the scope of regional government and/or non-governmental organizations that provide assistance.
25. Integrated Service Center hereinafter referred to as PPT is a generic term that can be used by various institutions that provide services for victims of violence such as Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, Safe House, Child Social Protection House, Trauma Center Protection House, Women's Social Protection House, Shelter, etc.
26. Minimum Service Standards hereinafter abbreviated as SPM is a performance benchmark for integrated service units in providing services for handling reports/complaints, health services, Social Rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal assistance, as well as Repatriation and social reintegration for Women and Children Victims of Violence. 27. Regional Action Plan is a foundation and guideline for relevant agencies, vertical agencies, and the community, in carrying out activities for the implementation of prevention and protection of women and children victims of violence.
28. Safe House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child in the womb.
8. Violence is any act against a person that results in suffering or pain physically, sexually, psychologically, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty.
9. 11. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, serious injury or disability to a person's body, miscarriage or unconsciousness and/or causes death.
12. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, distrust or severe psychological suffering to a person.
13. Sexual violence is any act in the form of forced sexual intercourse, sexual abuse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural and/or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
14. 25. I. GENERAL

Every citizen has the right to be free from torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and has the right to obtain a sense of security and freedom from all forms of violence. Violence is any act against a person that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty.

Women and children are groups vulnerable to experiencing violence. All forms of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity, therefore legal protection is needed to protect their dignity and to guarantee their right to life in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.

This view is based on Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia which states that "Every person has the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under their control, and has the right to a sense of security and protection from threats of fear to do or not do something which is a human right".

The Regional Government is obliged and responsible to implement efforts to protect women and children victims of violence through implementing protection policies for women and children victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence, establishing PPT, ensuring -2- the implementation of service facilities for victims, seeking effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and seeking the creation of cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Konawe Kepulauan Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of services, assistance, guidance, supervision, reporting and funding for women and children victims of violence in Konawe Kepulauan Regency.

I. GENERAL

Every citizen has the right to be free from torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and has the right to obtain a sense of security and freedom from all forms of violence. Violence is any act against a person that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty.

Women and children are groups vulnerable to experiencing violence. All forms of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity, therefore legal protection is needed to protect their dignity and to guarantee their right to life in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.

This view is based on Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia which states that "Every person has the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under their control, and has the right to a sense of security and protection from threats of fear to do or not do something which is a human right".

The Regional Government is obliged and responsible to implement efforts to protect women and children victims of violence through implementing protection policies for women and children victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence, establishing PPT, ensuring -2- the implementation of service facilities for victims, seeking effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and seeking the creation of cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Konawe Kepulauan Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is the Konawe Kepulauan Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of Konawe Kepulauan Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Konawe Kepulauan.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Konawe Kepulauan Regency.
5. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, -4- social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
6. Woman is a person who has female genitalia, can experience menstruation, pregnancy, childbirth, breastfeeding and includes persons who are legally recognized as Women.
7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child in the womb.
8. Violence is any act against a person that results in suffering or pain physically, sexually, psychologically, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty.
9. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or pain to women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or private life.
10. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in suffering or pain physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty.
11. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, serious injury or disability to a person's body, miscarriage or unconsciousness and/or causes death.
12. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, distrust or severe psychological suffering to a person.
13. Sexual violence is any act in the form of forced sexual intercourse, sexual abuse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural and/or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
14. Exploitation is an action with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or -5- body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain material or immaterial benefits.
15. Victim is a woman and child who experiences physical suffering, psychological suffering, sexual suffering, either directly or indirectly resulting from acts of violence.
16. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
18. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
19. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by Professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
20. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for strengthening victims of violence to resolve the problems they face.
21. Repatriation is an effort to return women and children victims of violence to their families or communities that can provide protection and fulfill their needs.
22. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions so that they can carry out their roles normally both in the family and in society.
23. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with their families, communities, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection and fulfill the needs of victims.
24. Institution is an agency/office/body/office within the scope of regional government and/or non-governmental organizations that provide assistance.
25. Integrated Service Center hereinafter referred to as PPT is a generic term that can be used by various institutions that provide services for victims of violence such as Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, Safe House, Child Social Protection House, Trauma Center Protection House, Women's Social Protection House, Shelter, etc.
26. Minimum Service Standards hereinafter abbreviated as SPM is a performance benchmark for integrated service units in providing services for handling reports/complaints, health services, Social Rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal assistance, as well as Repatriation and social reintegration for Women and Children Victims of Violence. 27. Regional Action Plan is a foundation and guideline for relevant agencies, vertical agencies, and the community, in carrying out activities for the implementation of prevention and protection of women and children victims of violence.
28. Safe House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards.

Article 14

1. In order to provide services and protection to women and children from violence, the Regional Government establishes an Integrated Service Center as a service center for women and children victims of violence.
2. The Integrated Service Center as referred to in paragraph (1), consists of elements of the Office of Population Control Family Planning Women's Protection and Child Protection, Health Office, Education and Culture Office, Social Office, Population and Civil Registration Administration Office, Community and Village Empowerment Office, Civil Service Police Unit, Regional General Hospital, Police Resort, Non-Governmental Organizations, and Universities.
3. The Integrated Service Center as referred to in paragraph (2), is established by Regent's Decree.
4. Further provisions regarding the organizational structure of the Integrated Service Center are regulated by Regent's Regulation.

Article 25

Guidance and supervision as referred to in Article 24 paragraph (2) and paragraph (3), are carried out in order to realize the objectives of implementing protection for women and children victims of violence in accordance with minimum service standards established by laws and regulations.

Article 28

1. The Regional Government may provide financial assistance to community organizations, social organizations, or non-governmental organizations and universities that implement protection for women and children victims of violence.
2. Financial assistance as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be in accordance with regional financial capacity and implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations in the field of regional finance.

Article 19

1. The Integrated Service Center in carrying out its duties and functions may coordinate with the Sub-district Integrated Service Center, and competent parties in making efforts to prevent violence against women and children.

14- (2) Further provisions regarding the mechanism for implementing prevention duties as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 18

Integrated Service CenterForms of prevention of violence against women and children carried out by the Integrated Service Center, can be implemented through:
a. socialization activities of laws and regulations to the community related to the protection of the rights of women and children; andb. training of Integrated Service Center members related to the implementation of their duties in preventing violence against children and women.

CHAPTER V

OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Article 10

Obligations and responsibilities in the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence are the shared responsibility of:
a. regional government;
b. society;
c. family and parents.

The obligations of family and parents as referred to in Article 10 letter c, who legally have full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence and protect women and children as part of family members.

I. GENERAL

Every citizen has the right to be free from torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and has the right to obtain a sense of security and freedom from all forms of violence. Violence is any act against a person that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty.

Women and children are groups vulnerable to experiencing violence. All forms of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity, therefore legal protection is needed to protect their dignity and to guarantee their right to life in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.

This view is based on Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia which states that "Every person has the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under their control, and has the right to a sense of security and protection from threats of fear to do or not do something which is a human right".

The Regional Government is obliged and responsible to implement efforts to protect women and children victims of violence through implementing protection policies for women and children victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence, establishing PPT, ensuring -2- the implementation of service facilities for victims, seeking effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and seeking the creation of cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Konawe Kepulauan Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of services, assistance, guidance, supervision, reporting and funding for women and children victims of violence in Konawe Kepulauan Regency.

Violence is any act against a person that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty.

Women and children are groups vulnerable to experiencing violence. All forms of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity, therefore legal protection is needed to protect their dignity and to guarantee their right to life in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.

This view is based on Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia which states that "Every person has the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under their control, and has the right to a sense of security and protection from threats of fear to do or not do something which is a human right".

The Regional Government is obliged and responsible to implement efforts to protect women and children victims of violence through implementing protection policies for women and children victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence, establishing PPT, ensuring -2- the implementation of service facilities for victims, seeking effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and seeking the creation of cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Konawe Kepulauan Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of services, assistance, guidance, supervision, reporting and funding for women and children victims of violence in Konawe Kepulauan Regency.

Article 14

1. In order to provide services and protection to women and children from violence, the Regional Government establishes an Integrated Service Center as a service center for women and children victims of violence.
2. The Integrated Service Center as referred to in paragraph (1), consists of elements of the Office of Population Control Family Planning Women's Protection and Child Protection, Health Office, Education and Culture Office, Social Office, Population and Civil Registration Administration Office, Community and Village Empowerment Office, Civil Service Police Unit, Regional General Hospital, Police Resort, Non-Governmental Organizations, and Universities.
3. The Integrated Service Center as referred to in paragraph (2), is established by Regent's Decree.
4. Further provisions regarding the organizational structure of the Integrated Service Center are regulated by Regent's Regulation.

b. access and information about the existence of complaint centers, PPT, and all matters related to the fulfillment of their rights and involvement in the decision-making process related to assistance and case development.
c. services that include medical, extensive medicolegal, psychosocial and legal.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is the Konawe Kepulauan Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of Konawe Kepulauan Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Konawe Kepulauan.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Konawe Kepulauan Regency.
5. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, -4- social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
6. Woman is a person who has female genitalia, can experience menstruation, pregnancy, childbirth, breastfeeding and includes persons who are legally recognized as Women.
7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child in the womb.
8. Violence is any act against a person that results in suffering or pain physically, sexually, psychologically, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty.
9. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or pain to women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or private life.
10. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in suffering or pain physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty.
11. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, serious injury or disability to a person's body, miscarriage or unconsciousness and/or causes death.
12. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, distrust or severe psychological suffering to a person.
13. Sexual violence is any act in the form of forced sexual intercourse, sexual abuse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural and/or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
14. Exploitation is an action with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or -5- body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain material or immaterial benefits.
15. Victim is a woman and child who experiences physical suffering, psychological suffering, sexual suffering, either directly or indirectly resulting from acts of violence.
16. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
18. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
19. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by Professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
20. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for strengthening victims of violence to resolve the problems they face.
21. Repatriation is an effort to return women and children victims of violence to their families or communities that can provide protection and fulfill their needs.
22. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions so that they can carry out their roles normally both in the family and in society.
23. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with their families, communities, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection and fulfill the needs of victims.
24. Institution is an agency/office/body/office within the scope of regional government and/or non-governmental organizations that provide assistance.
25. Integrated Service Center hereinafter referred to as PPT is a generic term that can be used by various institutions that provide services for victims of violence such as Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, Safe House, Child Social Protection House, Trauma Center Protection House, Women's Social Protection House, Shelter, etc.
26. Minimum Service Standards hereinafter abbreviated as SPM is a performance benchmark for integrated service units in providing services for handling reports/complaints, health services, Social Rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal assistance, as well as Repatriation and social reintegration for Women and Children Victims of Violence. 27. Regional Action Plan is a foundation and guideline for relevant agencies, vertical agencies, and the community, in carrying out activities for the implementation of prevention and protection of women and children victims of violence.
28. Safe House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards.

CHAPTER VIII

REPORTING

Article 26

c. services; andd. performance.
3. Submission of written reports as referred to in paragraph (2), shall be carried out at least once every 3 (three) months.

Funds for the implementation of protection of women and children victims of violence, are sourced from:
a. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget; andb. other lawful sources in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
